Keep the criterion anchored to progress toward the requested relation, not merely any book movement; the book appears altered/repositioned, but that alone is not progress. One nuance to investigate is that the edit changes the scene substantially (including the flower’s appearance/count and book presentation), so ensure the evaluator compares the correct target and reference across source and edited images before concluding absence. Do not treat the five repeated, high-confidence judgments as independent proof or infer missing progress from variation; there are no transport, schema, or dependency failures indicated.

The node’s absent judgment is well supported: the edited image shows the book and flowers separated, with no visible behind/occlusion relation. But its criterion says any movement of the book counts as partial, while the rubric explicitly excludes unrelated edits; the traces even note repositioning or alteration without progress toward the requested relation. Tighten the partial criterion to require observable movement toward placing the book behind the flower, and distinguish that from unrelated repositioning or object alteration. Preserve unknown for genuinely insufficient visual evidence. The repeated high-confidence absent traces and full aggregate agreement indicate no transport, schema, or dependency failure and do not justify changing the requested relation or forcing a different label.

The node’s binding and criterion are broadly sound, and the repeated valid traces support “absent”: the edited image shows the book and flowers separated, with no visible behind relation. For robustness, make the typed criterion explicitly compare source and edited states and count only observable movement of the identified book toward/behind the identified flower as partial progress; distinguish that from mere repositioning or object alteration.
